summary: Aroostook County, ME steel tower erected by the state in 1914 (48 ft in 1920); FFLA lists it standing with the cab no longer in place; no current access information found.

staffing.status: watchman J.M. Donahue named in 1917; no later staffing found

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1914 report gives fifty feet from the ground to the portable house; the 1920 inventory and Maine Memory give 48 feet. The record's 14.6 m (48 ft) follows the later figures; the 50 ft figure is read as the height to the lookout room.

notes_for_editor: The cab-gone status rests on one FFLA asterisk and has no date; no current photo or visit report was found. The 1920 inventory is cited through the Forest Lookouts transcription, not the original inventory. No access level is recorded because no source describes access; the site's land ownership is not stated in the sources read. Maine Memory photo credit and licence not recorded (no image URL verified). Facebook snippets about this watchman camp were seen in search results but not fetched, so they are not cited.
